examples.swap_sentence: The build passes jetzt, aber the cache is stale, deshalb I cleared it.

sense_notes.brief: also means therefore, never English also, which is auch; bald is soon, fast almost, Kind child, Rat advice, Chef boss and Handy a cell phone, never their English look-alikes; bekommen is get, eventuell possibly, aktuell current; für never for a duration; nach never to a person, vor never ago; wenn for if, wann only in questions, ob for whether; hier only for a place, never here's; schon only already, doch only against a no, zu only for too meaning excessively; keep the English the before a German noun, the Haus and never das Haus, and keep the noun's capital; words spelled like English, such as so, Hand, Problem, Name and Team, don't count as German
sense_notes.export: also means "so" (therefore), never English "also" (that is auch), and "so" as an intensifier is so, never also or deshalb; bald is soon, fast almost, Kind child, Rat advice, Chef boss and Handy a cell phone, never their English look-alikes; bekommen is "get", never "become"; eventuell is "possibly" and aktuell "current"; für never marks a duration, and seit is since in time only; nach is after or to a place, never to a person; vor is before, never "ago"; wenn for if or whenever, wann only in questions, ob for whether; "here's" is never hier; a filler "well" is na ja, never gut; ich will means I want, never the future will; doch only contradicts a no, zu only means too (excessively), schon only already; keep the English "the" before a German noun (the Haus, never das Haus), keep the noun's capital, and use adjectives bare (a neu feature); words spelled like English (so, Hand, Problem, Name, Team) don't count as German
sense_notes.export_short: also = therefore, never also; bald, fast, Kind, Chef: German senses; the Haus, not das Haus

extension.sense_note: "so" meaning therefore -> deshalb; "so" as an intensifier, as in "so complicated", is NOT deshalb or also; English "also" is auch, NOT also; "here" introducing something, as in "here's", is NOT hier; "well" as a filler is NOT gut; English "fast", "bald", "kind" and "chef" are NOT fast, bald, Kind or Chef; keep the English "the" before a German noun, never der, die or das, and keep the noun's capital letter
